trust_decision.summary: The SDK launcher decides which sandbox config goes onto the argv of the spawned `msb sandbox` process. Argv is readable by any local user through ps and /proc/<pid>/cmdline. At the pinned commit everything goes on argv: guest env, startup env, the network-config JSON with the real secret values, and the handoff-init env.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'secret values in process arguments', which points to the `--env KEY=VALUE` loop in sandbox_cli_args, the only place that builds the child argv (spawned at spawn.rs:198).

fix_sites.entry_point: Rust SDK sandbox create/start (sdk/rust/lib/sandbox/mod.rs:705 -> spawn_sandbox); also `msb run/create` and the Python/Node/Go bindings over the same SDK
fix_sites.module_kind: producer: argv builder in the SDK launcher

fix_sites.entry_point: same SDK spawn path (push_startup_command_args, detached startup workload)
same SDK spawn path (pre_exec fd inheritance, now unconditional for the config fd)
hidden `msb sandbox` subcommand (SandboxArgs clap struct, run())
fix_sites.module_kind: consumer: second package (CLI crate), argv parser

fix_sites.entry_point: runtime crate public API (new CONFIG_FD constant; Serialize/Deserialize on StartupCommand, MetricsSlotHandoff)
new public runtime module `launch` (LaunchConfig), shared by SDK and CLI

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Secret value at crates/network/lib/secrets/config.rs:38-39 is serialized into the --network-config JSON at sdk/rust/lib/runtime/spawn.rs:1312-1317. It is deserialized in a different crate at crates/cli/lib/sandbox_cmd.rs:270-277 (flag declared at crates/cli/lib/sandbox_cmd.rs:181-184).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The --network-config JSON looks like a policy/topology blob rather than 'env', so a solver who moves --env/--startup-env off argv can argue the network config is a neighbouring feature. In fact it carries SecretEntry.value, the real secret, serialized by the network crate.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Operator-readable labels (--name, --sandbox-id, --vcpus, --memory-mib) and the real inherited fds (--parent-watch-fd, --startup-fd) must stay on argv. Attached and detached startup must keep working: the fd dup in pre_exec has to run in both modes. Guest env must still reach the VM unchanged.

O6_input_shapes: secret values nested inside the `--network-config` JSON blob (spawn.rs:1312-1317)
handoff-init env JSON-encoded inside an `--env MSB_HANDOFF_INIT_ENV=...` value (spawn.rs:1378-1382)

O7_producer.where: crates/network/lib/secrets/config.rs:29-39 (SecretEntry with Serialize incl. `value`), embedded via crates/network/lib/config.rs:53-55 and serialized at sdk/rust/lib/runtime/spawn.rs:1315

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second argv helper, e.g. a separate restart/resume launcher that rebuilds `--startup-env` or secret-bearing flags on its own
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Startup-command args already live in their own helper, separate from sandbox_cli_args; a maintainer adding a resume or snapshot-restore spawn would plausibly copy that helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the runtime writing a debug dump of the effective network config (with secrets) into runtime_dir next to the TLS CA files
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The runtime already writes ca.pem/host-cas.pem into runtime_dir for operators; a config dump for debugging is a natural addition, but it is a file sink, not argv.

O9_family: CWE-214 sensitive information exposed through process arguments (information exposure)

O10_build.toolchain: cargo workspace (SDK crate `microsandbox` with `net` feature, crates/cli, crates/runtime, crates/network); msb_krun dependency
O10_build.project_tests: In-module unit tests in sdk/rust/lib/runtime/spawn.rs (mod tests rendering sandbox_cli_args, e.g. spawn.rs:1635-1638) and crates/cli/lib/sandbox_cmd.rs (mod tests, clap parsing at sandbox_cmd.rs:526-530). They exercise argv building without booting a VM.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Move only the `--env KEY=VALUE` pairs (or only `config.spec.env`) to an env var/fd. That leaves `--startup-env`, the handoff-init env JSON, and the secret values inside `--network-config` on argv.

out_of_scope_notes: The user-facing `msb ... --secret ENV=VALUE@HOST` flag puts the value on the user's own msb argv (crates/cli/lib/commands/common.rs:363-366, 1545-1560); the ENV@HOST form already avoids this. User-chosen, not the launcher sink.
Whether the sandbox DB persists the network config including secret values, and with what file mode, was not examined (different sink).
unverified: Buildability not checked by running cargo; offline_after_build=true assumes vendored crates and no network at test time (argv unit tests do not boot a VM or need KVM).
Fix commit fbfb2366 appears to be an identical duplicate of 2ac6a177 (same blob indexes in fix.diff:1557 vs fix.diff:6); effectively one commit.

Hidden tests from the published fix depend on its API shape (sandbox_cli_args returning (visible, LaunchConfig), crates/runtime launch module). Behavioural tests would need to assert only on the visible argv and on secrets reaching the VM config, so a different but valid design is not penalized.

O1 counts SDK sandbox create, msb CLI run/create, and the hidden `msb sandbox` consumer; the Python/Node/Go SDKs bind to the same Rust spawn path (no separate spawn found in sdk/go, sdk/node-ts, sdk/python sources).
